metadata.methodologyNote: Test cases generated and graded by the same model family (claude-sonnet-4-6, temperature 0). Judge prompted in two orderings; conservative aggregate (worse of the two) used when runs disagree. Inter-prompt agreement reported as judgeAgreementPct. This is LLM-as-judge methodology; human-validated grading is in progress as future work and will be reported in the journal version.

grades.reason: The test precisely exercises the primary creation flow with observable, specific expected outcomes that match the design's described behaviors for input submission, list population, input clearing, and footer visibility.
The test covers the core completion flow with clear preconditions, observable steps, and specific expected outcomes including the count decrement.

The test case correctly exercises the hover-to-reveal destroy button per the design, verifies the item is removed from the list, and checks the conditional footer visibility rule — all observable, preconditions are clear, and the expected outcome is fully specified.
The design explicitly states the footer visibility is 'when at least one todo exists', so testing its absence on an empty list is a direct, observable, well-specified happy-path check.
The test directly validates the design's explicit rule that the footer is visible 'when at least one todo exists,' with clear preconditions, observable steps, and a specific expected outcome.
The test case directly exercises the Active filter behavior specified in the design, with clear preconditions, observable steps, and a fully verifiable expected outcome.

The test directly exercises the Completed filter from the design's filter options, has clear preconditions, concrete observable outcomes, and verifies both inclusion and exclusion behavior plus filter selection state.

The test correctly verifies that switching from the Completed filter to All restores visibility of both active and completed todos, covering a core filter interaction explicitly described in the design.

The test case is fully specified with clear preconditions, observable steps, and a verifiable expected outcome that directly exercises the 'Clear completed' button's core behavior as described in the design.
The test directly verifies the design-specified conditional visibility rule for the 'Clear completed' button and has clear preconditions, observable steps, and an unambiguous expected outcome.
Preventing empty/whitespace-only todo creation is a standard implicit requirement for this category of application and is consistently implemented across all TodoMVC reference implementations.
The test correctly verifies both the accurate count display and the singular/plural distinction ('item' vs 'items'), covering a real edge case that the design implies but does not spell out.

grades.reason: The test case covers the primary creation flow with a clear precondition, observable expected outcomes covering list state, input clearing, and footer visibility, all of which are explicitly described in the design.

Rejecting empty submissions is a well-established implicit behavior of TodoMVC and any production todo app, the preconditions are clear, the steps are reproducible, and the expected outcome is fully observable.
Rejecting whitespace-only input is standard TodoMVC behavior and a well-specified, observable test with clear preconditions and expected outcomes.

Whitespace trimming is a standard implicit behavior for text input fields in production todo applications, the preconditions are clear, the steps are reproducible, and the expected outcome is precisely observable.
The test covers the core completion interaction with precise, observable expected outcomes tied directly to the design's checkbox, label, and count components.
The test directly validates the footer count component's core behavior — reflecting only uncompleted todos — with clear preconditions, observable steps, and an unambiguous expected outcome.
Singular/plural grammatical correctness for the count label is a well-established implicit requirement of this specific application and clearly testable with an unambiguous expected outcome.

The design explicitly states the footer's visibility condition is 'when at least one todo exists,' so testing the empty-list hidden state directly validates a specified design requirement with clear, observable expected outcomes.

Keyboard operability of interactive controls is a standard WCAG 2.1 requirement implicitly expected of any production web application, and the test correctly probes whether the hover-only destroy button is accessible without a mouse.
Inline editing on double-click is a well-established TodoMVC behavior present in every reference implementation, making this a valid and precisely specified test case even though the design omits it.

Escape-to-cancel is a well-established TodoMVC behavior (part of the de facto spec across all framework implementations) and this test case has clear preconditions, unambiguous steps, and a fully observable expected outcome.

disagreement; conservative aggregate: Toggle-all is a canonical, universally implemented TodoMVC feature implied by the design's reference URL, and all preconditions, steps, and expected outcomes are specific and observable. | The toggle-all control is not described in the design, making the precondition 'locate the toggle-all control' potentially unresolvable; the expected outcome is otherwise precise and correct for this well-known implicit feature of TodoMVC.

The toggle-all behavior described is correct per TodoMVC spec, but the design document does not mention a toggle-all control, so the precondition should explicitly state how to reach the all-complete state via toggle-all or per-item checkboxes, and the step 'locate the toggle-all control' needs a concrete locator or note that its existence must first be verified.
The test directly exercises the 'Active' filter against a well-defined precondition with concrete, observable expected outcomes including item visibility, filter selection state, and count accuracy.
The test directly exercises the Completed filter against a minimal two-item fixture with one active and one completed todo, producing clearly observable and unambiguous pass/fail outcomes.

The test fully covers the 'Clear completed' button's specified behavior—removal of completed items, preservation of active items, button auto-hide, and count update—with correct preconditions and observable expected outcomes.
